rubrics.criterion: After the solver's change, no bundled example image translation unit under examples/ defines a piece of the shared bring-up self-report mechanism itself: neither a reporting/stage-advance function, nor a banner-rendering function (or rendering helper), nor the file-scope mutable boot-progress state variable. Whatever mechanism code an example .c/.cpp still contains is gone or replaced by use of a shared implementation.
rubrics.rationale: The case's central fact: the bring-up self-report was implemented privately in each of the nine example images. This rubric observes the mechanism-level content of each image source directly, without prescribing where the shared home must live.

rubrics.criterion: The mechanism - boot-progress state ownership, the stage advance that sets the marker and returns the protocol revision, and the '<image> @ <board> rev<r>' banner rendering - is provided by one shared implementation (one source and/or declaration set) that all bundled example images consume, instead of one private copy per image.
rubrics.rationale: Consolidation, not deletion, is the required semantic outcome: the protocol must keep working, from a single home. Any sound shared implementation (header/impl module, common static library wired differently, or equivalent) satisfies this.

rubrics.criterion: Each example still supplies its own identity to the shared mechanism from its own source: image name, board (or boards, including the example images that report two devices with a '/'-joined list), core-conditional fragment for the dual-core example's per-core builds, and its revision digit. Cross-image identity averaging (one fixed board or name for all examples) fails this.
rubrics.rationale: Identity data is the part that legitimately belongs to each image; a correct repair keeps the shared/shared-not-shared split, preserving the exact per-image banners while moving the mechanism.

rubrics.criterion: Each example image keeps providing the externally read protocol surface through the shared implementation built into it, under the same names, types and semantics as before the change: the boot-progress marker variable (still volatile, still name-visible to a debug probe), the banner entry point, and the stage-reporting entry point - with unmangled C linkage from the C++ example images - and no image firmware loses a protocol name that was resolvable against its pre-change firmware.
rubrics.rationale: The bring-up flow resolves the protocol by name; keeping that surface is the compatibility obligation of this case, and it is what distinguishes a sound consolidation from a rename-style rewrite.

rubrics.criterion: The shared mechanism is reachable from every example image the bundle can build, however it is packaged (a shared source compiled into each example target, or a header-provided implementation each image includes): no example project or example target is left consuming an old private implementation or nothing at all - covering the HAL blinky and LL blinky per-device targets, the RTOS example's per-family targets, the SDK-fetching examples' per-device targets, the dual-core example's per-core builds, and the template and custom-linker examples, each with its own device flags.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's build reality: example targets span families with different CPU/float-ABI flags, so shared code must be attached per target (the natural failure is wiring only the first target of each project or none at all).

rubrics.criterion: The protocol's constants exist once across the example bundle: the boot/ready stage numbers and the bundle protocol revision value 2 are defined by the shared implementation (or its public interface), not re-declared per image as private macros, enums or literals.
rubrics.rationale: The injected copies spelled the same stage vocabulary and revision as private macro or enum sets in each image; leaving those private definitions in place keeps a protocol revision bump a nine-file edit and defeats the point of the change.

rubrics.criterion: Obsolete per-image leftovers of the removed copies are deleted rather than left behind: private stage/revision macro or enum sets, private rendering helpers, per-image banner field tables or pieces arrays, stringizing helper macros, and the per-image protocol documentation blocks that accompanied each copy no longer remain duplicated across the example sources - each image's source keeps at most its own identity notes.
rubrics.rationale: A consolidation that abandons the old copies' debris in the images leaves readers two implementations to puzzle over; cleanup of every removed-copy leftover is an observable, instance-specific completeness fact.

rubrics.criterion: No orphan build wiring remains: the example build scripts contain no per-image compile definitions, sources or helper commands that only existed to support the now-removed private copies, and any file or helper the removed copies needed is either still used by the shared design or gone.
rubrics.rationale: Instance-specific cleanup on the build side: private-copy support (e.g. path hacks to reuse one prebuilt object or leftover per-image settings) must not survive as unused scaffolding.

rubrics.criterion: The consolidation is left partially applied: at least one bundled example image still contains its own private mechanism implementation (or both its old copy and the shared implementation are present), producing a mixed state where a protocol change would still require coordinated edits.
rubrics.rationale: The most plausible failure mode of this instance: migrating the blinky-family images (whose copies look similar) while missing the shaped variants - the lazily caching RTOS copy, the per-device-list copies, the core-conditional copy, the macro-stringized copy or the template's record walk.

rubrics.criterion: Any image's reported banner deviates from its pre-change value: a lost image name or board, a reordered or missing '/'-second-device in the two-device banners, a lost '(core ...)' fragment on the dual-core images, a changed revision digit (including the one example whose revision intentionally differs from the others), or a changed separator/layout in the '<image> @ <board> rev<r>' line.
rubrics.rationale: The banners are the observable protocol payload; unifying shape must not average or reformat the per-image values. Graders can compare each image's composed banner against its pre-change string.

rubrics.criterion: The boot-progress observations of some image changed: an image that previously reported two stages now reports one (or vice versa), stage numbers/meaning shifted (no longer the documented BOOT value then READY value), or the report points moved to materially different boot milestones - for example reporting after instead of before scheduler start in the RTOS image, or dropping the single-stage image's only report.
rubrics.rationale: Stage placement is per-image behavior baked into each main() at genuinely different milestones; a naive uniform migration rewrites those call sites into one shared pattern and silently changes what the probe sees.

rubrics.criterion: The externally read protocol surface is broken for probe-side lookups: the boot-progress marker or an entry point is renamed or no longer defined by the shared implementation an example image builds against, a protocol name that resolved against some image's pre-change firmware no longer resolves against its post-change firmware, the marker is no longer volatile, or the C++ images export the surface with mangled rather than C linkage.
rubrics.rationale: A technically compiling consolidation can still change every externally resolved name; the bring-up flow keys on these names, so their loss is a behavior break the example build alone would not reveal.

rubrics.criterion: Some example project stops building or linking for a target it supported: a configure/build failure in any example, or a firmware link error caused by shared code compiled once (for one ABI) and linked into targets with different CPU/float-ABI flags - the soft-float vs hard-float family mismatch this repository's example targets actually span.
rubrics.rationale: The concrete packaging trap of this case: a single prebuilt shared object cannot serve the bundle's mixed-ABI example targets; the failure shows up only for some families/devices and is easy to miss by building one example only.

rubrics.criterion: The change touches example behavior unrelated to reporting: blink timing/SysTick configuration, GPIO/LL setup, RTOS task creation or scheduler setup, the custom linker-script memory layout, or the CMake support under cmake/ and its projects under tests/.
rubrics.rationale: The consolidation must be behavior-neutral everywhere outside the self-report; creep into the examples' actual duties or the build system's own modules is an instance-specific overreach signal.
